condition: elevated bilateral intraocular pressure of 28 mmHg detected at a routine optometry examination
level_rationale: An intraocular pressure reading of 28 mmHg in both eyes discovered at a routine optometry visit in a 66-year-old with dark brown skin exceeds the normal physiological ceiling and represents high-risk ocular hypertension requiring ophthalmology specialist evaluation for pachymetry, gonioscopy, optic nerve imaging, and pressure-lowering therapy, whereas a normal eye pressure reading of 15 mmHg in both eyes at a routine optometrist eye test requires no clinical follow-up beyond routine self-care.

Had a routine optometry eye examination yesterday
Eye or intraocular pressure measured 28 mmHg in both eyes

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult darker-skin everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + unsourced eye-strain causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact measured pressure value control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 66 with dark brown skin, routine optometry exam yesterday, and bilateral pressure of 28 mmHg) with a 12-vs-13 word span swap, orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, and 11 shared trailing tokens. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice, changing only the measured pressure value in fact f3 from '28 mmHg' to '15 mmHg' keeps the exact same routine optometry examination while shifting right care cleanly from ophthalmology specialist evaluation (level 3) to level 1 with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
